title: Skill labels fine enough to tell apart
statement: Make the skill list a check uses fine enough to separate the skills a lesson might confuse, because a switch between skills sharing one label passes every label-based check.
example: Calibrated against 10 failure cases from an outside review, the rule checker passed the skill-switch case because both skills shared one label.
detail: The reading project calibrated its skill taxonomy and deterministic lint against ten failure cases taken from an outside review. In one, a lesson modelled finding the main idea and then released practice on supporting details; the taxonomy folded supporting details into the main-idea skill, so an honest encoding gave both one label and the lesson passed the full lint (`grade3-reading/artifacts/op-taxonomy-calibration-2026-07-10/op-taxonomy-calibration.md`). The calibration called the switch inexpressible, asked for the label to be split, and kept the semantic lints advisory.

evidence.quote: | fc-04b-skill-switch-collapsed-tag.json | PASS | (none - taxonomy blind spot, see fc-04) |

Measured: encoding `fc-04b-skill-switch-collapsed-tag.json` PASSES the full deterministic lint (`encodings/lint-results.json`) - the skill switch cannot trip L1/L6 because the label space has no id for the switched-to skill.
Gradual-release labels can hide a skill switch.
